review_notes: I read the whole file and the tests in NormFormsTests/Coordinate.lean and NormFormsTests/DirectAPI.lean. I also grepped NormForms/CoordinateNormIteration.lean for uses. I did not read Mathlib simp sets in detail. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim that a loop or simp failure occurs. The only simp-tagged lemmas are `coordinateChange_apply` and `coordinateNorm_coordinateChange` (`simp↓`). I flag a missing canonical rule for evaluation, a missing simp attribute on the zero-iff lemma, and a definitional unfolding rule that competes with the real normal form. The evaluation and zero-iff findings point to downstream uses. The unfolding finding is more a design judgement. I propose no change to the orientation of the reindex, smul or change-of-basis lemmas.

findings.excerpt:
theorem coordinateNormPolynomial_eval (b : Basis ι K L) (x : ι → K) :
    MvPolynomial.eval x (coordinateNormPolynomial b) = coordinateNorm b x := by
findings.problem: This is the bridge from the polynomial to the coordinate norm. It is not a simp lemma, so no canonical normal form exists for `eval x (coordinateNormPolynomial b)`. The file's own consequences (`coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_eq_zero_iff`, `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_coordinateChange`) and the reindex lemma are all stated through it. Clients must write `rw [coordinateNormPolynomial_eval]` by hand before simp can use the norm lemmas. The tests repeat this pattern: `rw [coordinateNormPolynomial_eval]` followed by `simp [coordinateNorm]`, and `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval _ _` is used as a term. The orientation (polynomial evaluation to `coordinateNorm`) is terminating and cannot cycle, because `coordinateNorm` is a definition that is not simp-unfolded.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval` with `@[simp]`. Together with `@[simp]` on `coordinateNorm_eq_zero_iff` (and `coordinateNorm_coordinateChange` which is already `simp↓`), simp would then close `eval x (coordinateNormPolynomial b) = 0 ↔ x = 0` and `eval (coordinateChange b b' x) (coordinateNormPolynomial b) = eval x (coordinateNormPolynomial b')`. After that, `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_eq_zero_iff` and `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_coordinateChange` would be redundant as simp lemmas and should not also be tagged. The proofs inside the file that `rw` this lemma (`coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_eq_zero_iff`, `coordinateNorm_reindex`) are unaffected. `simp [h]` in `coordinateNormPolynomial_ne_zero` rewrites `eval x 0` and does not hit this lemma.
findings.benefit: Users can reduce statements about the norm form to statements about `coordinateNorm` with plain `simp`. The tests' manual `rw [coordinateNormPolynomial_eval]` step before `simp [coordinateNorm]` goes away.

findings.excerpt:
theorem coordinateNorm_eq_zero_iff (b : Basis ι K L) (x : ι → K) :
    coordinateNorm b x = 0 ↔ x = 0 := by
findings.problem: This is a standard `_eq_zero_iff` normal-form lemma: its left side is a simple head-symbol pattern and its right side is strictly simpler. It is not `@[simp]`, although the file already tags the neighbouring lemma `coordinateNorm_coordinateChange`. The same applies to `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_eq_zero_iff` (line 112), which duplicates this lemma through the eval bridge. As a result, simp cannot decide `coordinateNorm b x = 0` for the file's main definition. The proofs of `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_eq_zero_iff` and `coordinateNormPolynomial_ne_zero` and the downstream use in `CoordinateNormIteration` have to cite the lemma by name.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `coordinateNorm_eq_zero_iff`. Pair this with the `@[simp]` on `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval` from the previous finding, so that `coordinateNormPolynomial_eval_eq_zero_iff` becomes derivable by simp and need not be tagged separately. This avoids two competing rules for `eval … = 0`. The `x = 0` side has no `coordinateNorm` and cannot loop.
findings.benefit: Simp can use non-vanishing of the norm without the user supplying the lemma name. The simp set then has a canonical form for zero tests on both the norm and the norm polynomial.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem coordinateChange_apply (b : Basis ι K L) (b' : Basis κ K L) (x : κ → K) :
    coordinateChange b b' x = b.equivFun (b'.equivFun.symm x) :=
  rfl
findings.problem: This `@[simp]` lemma is just the definitional unfolding of `coordinateChange`. It makes simp expand every `coordinateChange b b' x` into `b.equivFun (b'.equivFun.symm x)`, which discards the abstraction the API is built around. It competes with the real structural rule `coordinateNorm_coordinateChange`, which has to be marked `@[simp↓]` so that it fires before the unfolding. Without the pre-rewrite flag, the unfolding would turn the argument into `b.equivFun (…)`. The lemma would then no longer match the rule, which has the shape `coordinateNorm b (coordinateChange b b' x)`. The docstring also says the lemma states that the element is unchanged. That is not what the statement says. Downstream, the tests do not rely on this simp lemma. `complex_swap_coordinates` still writes `simp [coordinateChange]`, so the unfolding is requested explicitly there as well.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `coordinateChange_apply`. Keep it as a plain lemma for explicit `rw` or `simp [coordinateChange_apply]` (the tests' `simp [coordinateChange]` already covers the opt-in case). Then downgrade `coordinateNorm_coordinateChange` to an ordinary `@[simp]`, since nothing competes with it. Fix the docstring to say it unfolds the definition. If the unfolding is kept as a simp lemma, document why `simp↓` is needed. I have not verified how this interacts with `coordinateChangePolynomial_eval`, whose right side contains `coordinateChange b b' x i`.
findings.benefit: Terms built from `coordinateChange` stay in their abstract form under simp. The simp set no longer depends on pre/post rewrite priority to keep `coordinateNorm_coordinateChange` applicable. Users opt into the unfolding when they want it.
